name: Mate in one
goal: You can tell checkmate from check, and find a mate in one move when there is one.
intro: Checkmate ends the game: the king is in check and there is no way out. It cannot move to a safe square, the check cannot be blocked, and the checking piece cannot be taken. If even one of those ways is open, it is only check, so look at every check you have and test each one.

parts.title: Check or mate?
parts.keyIdea: Not every check is mate: test each check for an escape square, a block and a capture.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's queen has just moved to c6. Your queen can give check in several ways, but only one of them is mate. For each check, ask where the king could go and whether Black could block or capture.

notes.text: Qf8, the queen to f8, gives check along the back rank (the row Black's king started on). The king cannot go to g8 or g7, because the queen covers both, and h7 holds its own pawn. Black's queen cannot block on g8 or take on f8, so it is mate. Compare Qc8+, which is only check: Black's queen simply takes yours.

parts.title: The queen and a helper
parts.keyIdea: The queen can mate right next to the king when another piece guards it.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's queen has just taken your pawn on c4. One of your checks is mate: find it.

notes.text: The queen takes the g7 pawn and checks the king. The king cannot take the queen, because your rook on g2 guards g7, and the king has nowhere to run: the queen covers g8 and h7. Checkmate.

parts.title: Six checks, one mate
parts.keyIdea: When you have many checks, test each one: a check that can be blocked or captured is only check.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black's king has just stepped from b8 to c8. Your queen can give check in six different ways, but only one of them is mate. Test each one.

notes.text: The queen checks the king along the back rank. The king cannot go to b8, b7 or c7, because your queen and your bishop on f4 cover them, and its own pieces fill d7 and d8. Nothing can block on b8 or take the queen, so it is mate. The other checks all leave a way out: Black takes the queen after Qc6+ or Qxd7+, and blocks Qa6+, Qc4+ or Qc2+ with the queen.

parts.title: A crowded king
parts.keyIdea: A king hemmed in by its own pieces can be mated by a lone knight, because a knight's check cannot be blocked.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White. Black has just taken your queen on f5. You have only a knight left to attack with, but look at how Black's own pieces crowd the king on h8.

notes.text: The knight jumps to f7 and checks the king. Every square next to the king holds a black piece, a knight's check cannot be blocked, and nothing can take the knight on f7. This is called a smothered mate.
